title: Ring protocol records
notes: The data model is not on a ring. Core calls ta_datamodel_vtable synchronously, as today (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/data-model.md). Only its results cross the rings, as value references.

Definition management uses request/result records. Native calls create and destroy the system, expose its rings, drive execution and install data model/value integrations. An attached debugger takes exclusive ownership of the whole system from the production pump. Inspection, abandonment and operator transitions use native primitives outside the production rings; no operator ring is added (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/debugging.md).

A vref in a c2h record is a reference core retained for the host. The host releases it when it has used the record. A vref in an h2c record transfers one retained reference to core at commit. Core releases it on refusal, drop or completion; a bounce returns status, not ownership. Host retry originals belong in a bounded submission table.

Replay seeds new execution: supplied inputs derive configuration and data model values, which may differ from an earlier run. External effects are suppressed while seeding. In live execution the host may execute effects on receipt, independently of recording, persistence or c2h.macrostep_ended.

common_flags.name: replaying
common_flags.doc: part of a replay (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/recording-and-replay.md). On c2h and tel: written by a replaying session. On h2c: an input of a replay; under a whole-system replay every h2c record carries it, sessions it spawns replay, mail between them is delivered as envelopes, and effects that would leave the process are suppressed until h2c.publish

common_flags.name: recorded

rings.name: h2c
rings.when_full: The host cannot post. It refuses at its edge (for example HTTP 503) or keeps the input itself. Core never waits on h2c.
rings.doc: Host requests, in host order. An event that cannot be admitted is consumed and bounced after its refusal output is reserved. Admission is not an execution barrier. Definition requests run between macrosteps without an envelope (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/definitions.md).

rings.name: c2h
rings.when_full: Before an action that may write c2h evaluates anything, core checks for room for the largest record. Without it the slot parks before the action, which runs once, after the host drains. Other slots go on. Core starts a macrostep only when c2h has room for all mandatory observations, cancellations, autoforwards, completion and end reports, including wrap padding. Startup and control phases can yield between macrosteps.
rings.doc: Everything that leaves the process or must not be lost: effects for I/O processors and invokers, macrostep end reports, bounces, load requests, images, and the inputs of recorded sessions.

rings.name: tel
rings.when_full: The record is dropped and counted. The next tel.dropped says how many. Telemetry never slows the system.
rings.doc: Observability: the trace records of core ADR 0067 under core's kind masks and sampling (core ADR 0073). Never used for replay.

messages.doc: The header `at` is the new time. It never moves back. Delayed sends due by then become runnable envelopes, in due order, then send order. Applied between macrosteps. Admission of an earlier event does not ensure that event has finished; the host awaits input_completed before posting time when it requires that execution order.

messages.summary: An external event for a session
messages.doc:
Header `session` names a resident session, or is 0 and `target` gives an address. Admitted into the pool when the pool is below its watermark. An event for an unloaded address waits in the pool and core asks for the session with c2h.load_needed. A capacity refusal consumes and bounces the record, allowing later controls to progress.

A live input runs at system time when taken; its header at does not advance that clock. A replay input moves its prepared session clock at take. Complete event metadata must also fit the expanded c2h.input. Service events carry invocation_seq, checked again at take. Zero means ordinary input, or an application-supplied replay seed.

A trace parent travels with the event (core ADRs 0067, 0073). A host that receives a traceparent header parses it (core's native ta_traceparent_parse) and fills the trace fields. The macrostep that takes the event runs under that context, with the cause key {session 0, macrostep parent_span_id}. An all-zero trace ID means no context. The envelope keeps the trace parent until take (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/envelope.md).

messages.doc:
With the replaying flag the session is prepared to replay (core ADR 0089): its clock starts at `clock`, it crosses no border, and it is published with h2c.publish. Inputs seed new configuration and data model values; exact restoration is not promised.

With `state`, a checkpoint (c2h.state, core ADR 0091) seeds the session, which replays with its clock starting at the state's; the c2h.input records after the checkpoint follow. This is how new execution starts from a checkpoint after a restart (core ADR 0105); exact restoration is not promised. h2c.load is not: it only pages a session back into memory within one process.

The trace fields are the trace parent the bootstrap macrostep runs under, as for h2c.event. When it answers c2h.load_needed and has none, the bootstrap runs under the trace parent of the first envelope waiting for the address.

messages.summary: End a replay and put the session on the route
messages.doc:
Held delayed sends due by `at` are dropped; the rest stay in the pool under their due times (core ADR 0094). Active invocations are retired with error.communication.invoke.<id>.unavailable.

An empty `address` publishes every replaying session at once: the end of a whole-system replay (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/recording-and-replay.md).

Refuses without mutation while supplied seed inputs remain pending. Generated local mail need not drain: pending mail follows the selected publication cut into live execution. Publication does not execute effects suppressed during seeding.

fields.doc: the time chosen for the seeded session

messages.doc:
Usually the answer to c2h.load_needed. Its delayed sends rejoin the pool. Waiting envelopes for it become runnable.

Loading only bounds memory; it is not persistence. The image is one c2h.unloaded wrote in this process, and it is valid only here (core ADR 0074). To seed new execution after a restart, use h2c.spawn with `state` (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/unloading.md).

Stage the complete restore outside macrosteps. Capacity or decoding failure leaves residency, timers and waiting mail unchanged. The host pins image until c2h.loaded or c2h.bounced correlates this request. Zero request_seq is refused when an active load request exists for the address.

messages.doc: Every envelope waiting for the address is recycled: mail becomes error.communication for its sender, in the same envelope (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/envelope.md, "Recycling"); external inputs receive c2h.input_refused and DEAD_LETTER telemetry. Large waiting lists are processed incrementally between macrosteps as c2h space permits.

messages.doc:
Header `session` is the invoking session. The trace fields are the trace parent the report's macrostep runs under, as for h2c.event; an invoker usually copies the context and span ID of its c2h.invoke.

Done enters the external queue with invoke metadata for finalize; errors are platform/internal events without event invokeid. A stale live instance cannot change a later invocation with the same authored ID.

messages.doc: A session that holds a macrostep slot, running or parked, has its execution abandoned first (core ADR 0082): c2h.macrostep_ended and c2h.input_completed say abandoned, then the session is destroyed.

messages.summary: Compile and register a complete definition
messages.doc:
Header session is 0. One atomic request, with no builder operations. The binding builds a native ta_scxml_spec with core's spec builder; core compiles it through the existing compiler and registers it between macrosteps. There is no byte layout of a spec. Native data model callbacks remain synchronous (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/definitions.md).

The host keeps spec valid and diagnostic writable until the correlated c2h.definition_result. Failure registers nothing and retains nothing from the submitted spec.

fields.name: spec
fields.doc: process-local handle of a complete native ta_scxml_spec built by the binding

fields.name: datamodel
fields.doc: process-local handle of a native-installed data model adapter

fields.name: diagnostic
fields.doc: host memory, owned and bounded by the host, that core writes core ADR 0058's native compile-error struct (ta_compile_error) into

messages.doc: Core ADR 0077 semantics: an unused definition is freed when its last hold, actor and nesting reference goes. Header session is 0.

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: the system-local definition ID returned by registration

messages.doc: Core ADR 0043 semantics: existing actors keep running; new spawns cannot use it. Retirement drops registration holds and is idempotent for an issued ID, including after it was freed. Header session is 0.

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: the system-local definition ID

messages.summary: Take back an admitted input that has not been taken
messages.doc:
Header session is 0. A control: it takes no envelope and is applied when read, also while core is not admitting. target_seq names an earlier h2c.event or h2c.invoke_report. If that input waits in the pool (runnable or on a waiting list), core unlinks and frees its envelope, releases its transferred values and name text, and writes c2h.input_refused with reason withdrawn. Core reserves that record before consuming the withdrawal (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/envelope.md).

If the input is no longer waiting, the withdrawal changes nothing and writes nothing: the input already has, or will get, its own single terminal record (c2h.bounced, c2h.input_refused or c2h.input_completed). A taken input, including one paused inside its macrostep, is never withdrawn; stopping it is an operator abandon (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/debugging.md). A target_seq not lower than this record's own seq is bounced as invalid.

fields.name: target_seq
fields.doc: the h2c seq of the input to withdraw

messages.summary: Declare an I/O processor or invoker type
messages.doc:
Header session is 0. A control: it takes no envelope and is applied when read. Every record after it sees the type declared, so replay sees the same declarations at the same points. Core keeps only the name: the implementation is the binding's, reached through c2h.send or c2h.invoke, c2h.invoke_cancel and c2h.invoke_forward.

Core checks a <send type> against the io registry and an <invoke type> against the invoker registry when the action runs. An undeclared type is error.execution in the chart, which the host could not raise later from c2h. Declaring a declared type changes nothing and writes nothing. A name core owns (scxml and its URI aliases) is bounced as reserved_type; failing to store the name is bounced as allocation. A declared type cannot be withdrawn.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: the type name as bytes; interned as an atom when declared

messages.doc:
For a recorded session this is the first record of its log.

Creation does not imply bootstrap and invocation startup have settled. c2h.input_completed correlates that completion with the originating spawn.

fields.name: parent
fields.doc: the invoking session, or 0

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.spawn, or 0 for an <invoke>

messages.summary: A recorded session took an input
messages.doc:
Written when a recorded session takes an envelope, before any effect of the macrostep it starts. These observations, fed back as h2c.event and h2c.invoke_report under h2c.spawn(replaying), seed a new execution. Recording imposes no persistence-before-effects rule.

Not written for an input a replaying session takes: that input is already in the log being replayed. A session seeded from c2h.state and replayed starts writing c2h.input again after h2c.publish.

Data is a copy_out snapshot created before binding or running the input, including finalize and autoforward. Later chart mutations cannot change it.

The trace fields are the trace parent the macrostep runs under, in h2c.event's form, so a journal keeps it and a replay fed back as h2c.event runs under the same trace ID and parent span. For mail and timers, parent_span_id is the span ID of the sending step: the cause's step key becomes a host cause with the same span ID.

messages.summary: A send for an I/O processor
messages.doc:
Mail to a local session never appears here: it is an envelope (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/envelope.md). A delayed send to an I/O processor waits in the pool and is written when due. The host may execute the send on receipt, without waiting for c2h.macrostep_ended or persistence.

A delayed send that becomes due on h2c.time is written outside any macrostep: its `macrostep` is 0, no end report follows, and the host may act on it at once. An end report would describe a macrostep that does not exist (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/envelope.md, "A due send to an I/O processor has no macrostep end").

The trace fields are the sending step's trace context and span ID (core ADR 0067), so the processor writes a traceparent header (version 00, trace ID, span_id, trace_flags) without calling into core. A delayed send keeps them in its envelope and carries the step that sent it, not the h2c.time that made it due.

messages.summary: Autoforward an event to an invocation
messages.doc:
Every event field is preserved at the autoforward point. Finalize runs first, as in the SCXML algorithm; each recipient then receives its own copy_out data before transition code runs. Record space is mandatory; a data-model copy failure remains error.execution.

The trace fields are the context and span ID of the forwarding step, as for c2h.send.

messages.doc: Everything the macrostep wrote to c2h comes before this record. The host may already have executed effects on receipt. This record reports that execution ended and gives its status, including abandonment; invocation startup may follow. It is neither input completion nor a durability acknowledgement (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/macrostep.md, "The macrostep end").

fields.name: source_seq
fields.doc: originating h2c input, including internal startup follow-up; 0 for local work

fields.name: effects
fields.doc: records this macrostep wrote to c2h, this end report excluded

fields.name: mail
fields.doc: envelopes it put in the pool

messages.summary: Call core back at this time
messages.doc: The earliest due delayed send in the pool changed. One timer in the host's event loop is enough.

flags.name: none
flags.doc: nothing is due: cancel the timer

messages.summary: An h2c record was not run
messages.doc: Core consumes the record, releases transferred values and keeps nothing of it. The host decides whether to retry using its own retained original. Reserve the bounded reply before consuming the request. This is terminal before admission; an admitted input instead ends in refused or completed.

messages.summary: Envelopes wait for an unloaded address
messages.doc:
Written once per address until h2c.load or h2c.load_failed answers it.

For a family whose first message creates the actor, h2c.spawn answers it.

fields.name: waiting
fields.doc: envelopes waiting for it

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.load

messages.doc:
The image holds the session's state and its delayed sends. The host keeps it, and wake_at, in its own index of unloaded sessions, and posts h2c.load when wake_at comes.

The image bounds memory; it is not a checkpoint. It is valid only in the process that wrote it and ends with it. c2h.state is the checkpoint.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.unload

fields.name: image_bytes
fields.doc: complete valid bytes written into the requested sink

fields.name: wake_at
fields.doc: its earliest delayed send

messages.summary: A recorded session's state at a point of its log
messages.doc:
A checkpoint (core ADR 0091). Its delayed sends are inside the image, so it is one artifact. Replaying from it needs only the c2h.input records after input_seq.

Unlike the image c2h.unloaded writes, it is meant to be stored. h2c.spawn `state` seeds new execution from it (core ADR 0105).

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.checkpoint

fields.name: image_bytes
fields.doc: complete valid bytes written into the requested sink

fields.name: input_seq
fields.doc: the last c2h.input it includes

messages.doc: For an empty-address publication, one session-0 result summarizes the atomic mode change for all replaying sessions.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.publish

fields.name: replayed
fields.doc: inputs it replayed; total for all-session publication

fields.name: dropped_timers
fields.doc: held delayed sends due by `at`

messages.summary: A session reached a top-level final state
messages.doc: Mail to a local parent (done.invoke) is an envelope; this record is for the host's books.
Envelopes still waiting for it are recycled as for h2c.load_failed.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.destroy, or 0 for execution-driven destruction

messages.doc:
Exactly one result per definition request. Header session is 0. Core reserves room for this fixed-size reply before consuming the request or changing definition state. No macrostep end report follows.

A compile_error diagnostic is the native ta_compile_error struct (core ADR 0058), written whole into the request's diagnostic memory with its code, path, subject, subject range, related text and message; no pointer into the spec or core escapes. If it does not fit, the status is capacity and nothing partial is written. The host owns the memory before and after completion (docs/proposals/ring-proto/reference/definitions.md).

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the definition request’s h2c seq

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: on successful register: the definition ID; otherwise 0

fields.name: diagnostic_bytes
fields.doc: bytes written to the request’s diagnostic buffer; 0 without a compile error

messages.summary: An admitted host input was not taken
messages.doc: Exactly one terminal refusal for an admitted h2c.event or invoke_report discarded by load failure, destruction, stale-instance validation, snapshot failure or an h2c.withdraw. No input observation or completion follows. Core releases its transferred values; host retry originals remain host-owned.

fields.name: source_seq
fields.doc: the originating h2c input

messages.summary: A host input and its startup follow-up settled
messages.doc: Exactly one terminal result for a taken host input, including spawn bootstrap. Emitted after stabilization and invocation-startup internal follow-up settle, regardless of recording or replaying flags. Earlier macrostep ends do not settle the host operation. This does not hold effects, await child-service completion or acknowledge persistence.

fields.name: source_seq
fields.doc: the originating h2c input

fields.name: macrostep
fields.doc: the last macrostep in the input execution

flags.name: ignored
flags.doc: the input event enabled no transition, so the chart ignored it (core ADR 0089 section 8). A request/response I/O processor answers its client at once instead of waiting for a timeout (docs/proposals/ring-proto/scenarios/S12-http-request.md)

messages.summary: A load-failure response finished recycling waiting inputs
messages.doc: Acknowledges h2c.load_failed after all waiting envelopes were recycled or refused. Each external input refusal precedes this result. Recycling may yield between macrosteps to drain c2h; its cursor uses the existing waiting list. A stale attempt receives bounced instead.

fields.name: cause_seq
fields.doc: the h2c.load_failed

fields.name: request_seq
fields.doc: the answered c2h.load_needed

messages.doc:
One ta_trace_record, kind for kind; only the fields its kind names are meaningful, and the rest are 0, or UINT32_MAX for a state, transition, action or expression that is none. The record is self-contained (core ADR 0098): names, values and the fault are text in its tail, beside the IDs they name, so a reader needs no live system. Values are text the data model renders (value_text), cut at the parameter telemetryValueBytes; vrefs never go on a lossy ring. Header `session` and `at` are the step key's session and the logical time; wall_ns is when it happened.

The step key is header `session`, `macrostep` and `microstep`. There is no span ID field: a span ID is a fixed 64-bit mix of the step key (core ADR 0067, ta_step_key_span_id), the same in every reader.

The lists are two spans: list_ids holds the u32 IDs of the transitions, then the exited, entered and history states, then the states the kind names, back to back, as many as the five counts say; list_names holds, in the same order, each entry's name as a u32 length and its UTF-8 bytes. list_ids comes first in the tail, so its IDs are 4-byte aligned and a reader can use them in place. When the record would not fit maxRecordBytes, core keeps the lists whole from the first and cuts the last list first; the counts say how many entries are there, not how many there were.

fields.name: wall_ns
fields.doc: the host clock when core wrote the record: wall-clock nanoseconds since the Unix epoch; 0 when the host installed no clock

fields.name: macrostep
fields.doc: with header session and microstep, the step key; 0 outside a macrostep

fields.name: cause_session
fields.doc: the session of the step that caused this one; 0 for a host-delivered cause

fields.name: cause_macrostep
fields.doc: the macrostep of the causing step; with cause_session 0, the host's parent span ID (W3C parent-id), or 0

fields.name: actor
fields.doc: the session's runtime actor ID, or 0

fields.name: definition
fields.doc: the definition's ID

fields.name: send
fields.doc: the send ID's handle, for SENT and its kin; send_id is its text

fields.name: invoke
fields.doc: the invocation's handle, for INVOKED and its kin; invoke_id is its text

fields.name: microstep
fields.doc: from 1 per macrostep; 0 for the macrostep itself

fields.name: cause_microstep
fields.doc: the microstep of the causing step; with cause_session and cause_macrostep, the cause's step key, whose span ID is the parent span

fields.name: state
fields.doc: the state at the record's position

fields.name: transition
fields.doc: the transition at the record's position

fields.name: action
fields.doc: the action at the record's position

fields.name: iteration
fields.doc: the <foreach> iteration at the record's position; on FOREACH, the iteration it names

fields.name: subject_state
fields.doc: the state the kind names: a final state, a guard's source, a <data>'s owner, an operator transition's source

fields.name: subject_action
fields.doc: the action the kind names: ACTION_FAILED's

fields.name: expr
fields.doc: the expression the kind names

fields.name: dropped
fields.doc: ABANDONED: the internal events it discarded

fields.name: fault_code
fields.doc: the fault’s code, with fault_detail

fields.name: transition_count
fields.doc: transitions in list_ids

fields.name: exited_count
fields.doc: exited states in list_ids

fields.name: entered_count
fields.doc: entered states in list_ids

fields.name: history_count
fields.doc: history states in list_ids

fields.name: state_count
fields.doc: states the kind names in list_ids: a configuration, or an operator transition's targets

fields.name: trace_kind
fields.doc: ta_trace_kind

fields.name: position
fields.doc: ta_trace_at

fields.name: trace_flags
fields.doc: the trace context’s flags (sampled)

fields.name: trace_detail
fields.doc: the trace context’s detail (watched)

fields.name: runaway_cause
fields.doc: RUNAWAY only: what stopped the input

fields.name: event_type
fields.doc: the event's type

fields.name: list_ids
fields.doc: the u32 IDs of the lists, back to back (see above)

fields.name: session_id
fields.doc: the session's ID as text, as _sessionid holds it

fields.name: cause_session_id
fields.doc: the causing session's ID as text; empty when there is no cause

fields.name: address
fields.doc: the session’s family/name, when it has a named address

fields.name: family_name
fields.doc: the definition's family, on the kinds that open a run

fields.name: revision
fields.doc: the definition's revision, on the kinds that open a run

fields.name: document_name
fields.doc: the definition's document name, on the kinds that open a run

fields.name: source
fields.doc: where the definition's first state was written, on the kinds that open a run

fields.name: state_name
fields.doc: the name of `state`

fields.name: transition_name
fields.doc: the name of `transition`

fields.name: action_name
fields.doc: the name of `action`

fields.name: subject_state_name
fields.doc: the name of `subject_state`

fields.name: subject_action_name
fields.doc: the name of `subject_action`

fields.name: name
fields.doc: the name the kind carries: a <data>'s

fields.name: event_name
fields.doc: the event's dotted name

fields.name: event_send_id
fields.doc: the event's sendid

fields.name: event_invoke_id
fields.doc: the event's invokeid

fields.name: event_data
fields.doc: the event's data as text, cut at telemetryValueBytes

fields.name: send_id
fields.doc: the send ID, for SENT and its kin

fields.name: invoke_id
fields.doc: the invoke ID, for INVOKED and its kin

fields.name: value_text
fields.doc: the kind's value as text, cut at telemetryValueBytes

fields.name: fault_detail
fields.doc: the fault’s error event name

fields.name: fault_data
fields.doc: the fault's data as text, cut at telemetryValueBytes

fields.name: list_names
fields.doc: the names of the list entries (see above)

flags.name: truncated
flags.doc: something was cut: a value, the event's data, a list, or a name, to fit telemetryValueBytes or maxRecordBytes

flags.name: suppressed
flags.doc: an effect a replaying session did not perform

flags.name: event
flags.doc: the event_* fields hold the event the kind names

flags.name: value
flags.doc: the kind carries a value; value_text holds its text unless telemetryValueBytes is 0

flags.name: fault
flags.doc: the fault_* fields hold the kind's fault

flags.name: lists_cut
flags.doc: a list was cut to fit maxRecordBytes

fields.name: first_seq
fields.doc: the seq the first dropped record would have had
